lines.text: Ilse would be the Stone. She had measured people by touch for twenty years. If she could feel anything in me when she took my hand, the Stone would too.
Again. I can feel you from here. So could Vance, from the other side of the river.
The first day, I poured too little. The second day, I poured into the wrong thread.
Wren lit up like a bonfire. Her hair stood straight up. Her next arrow went through the target, the wall, and the stable behind it.
Not me! Not me! Point it at the dog!
On the third day, I found Ash's thread, and pushed.
Ash glowed. Not a little. All of him. Like a dog made of moonlight.
Is... is that dog glowing?
No.
Right. Right you are, sir.
Every time, the frost came up my fingers. By the fourth day, my hands were wrapped in bandages, and Ilse's spectacles frosted over whenever she held them.
I've added it to the accounts, my lord. One table, frozen. Two chairs, frozen. One innkeeper's nerves.
Ash didn't mind at all. He thought it was the best game anyone had ever invented. Every time it was over, he brought me a stick.
On the fifth night, I stopped pushing. I thought of Ash the day I found him, in the ruined kennel, too weak to stand. And I just let go, the way you let go of a breath.
Ilse took my hand, and closed her eyes, and was quiet for a long time.
Nothing.
I feel nothing at all. Lucan, you're as empty as the day they measured you.
Behind me, Ash sat glowing softly in the dark, very pleased with himself. Tamsin was crying. Wren pretended she wasn't.
Then there was a sharp crack, like ice on a pond.
Under Ash's paws, the old flagstone had split clean through, from one side to the other.
It has to go somewhere, Lucan. Everything you pour into him. It has to go somewhere.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter seventy-seven, coming soon.
